title: Decouple in-flight window manager and add per-tenant circuit breaker for async ingress
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our existing async ingress/worker loop combines in-flight window accounting, retry scheduling, and downstream prefetching in a single hot path. This has caused several operational problems: 1) noisy tenants can exhaust worker capacity and create head-of-line blocking for other tenants; 2) the combined code-path is hard to reason about and is a recurring source of subtle bugs when we change retry semantics; 3) performance regressions have been observed after dependency upgrades to the Redis client.

Goals:
- Split the in-flight window (the number of outstanding tokenized tasks per worker) into a separate, testable component with a clear API so it can be reused across Redis Stream and Kafka consumers.
- Introduce a per-tenant circuit breaker with configurable thresholds (error rate, p95 queue latency, outstanding tasks) to protect from noisy neighbors and improve fairness.
- Move to a credit-based backpressure model between ingress and workers (credit offers rather than naive semaphore grants) to reduce head-of-line blocking and improve tail latency.
- Rework retry semantics: adopt idempotency-token-aware retries and move retry scheduling off the hot path into a lightweight timer wheel / delayed queue that is observable and bounded.
- Address dependency compatibility: validate and, where needed, upgrade Redis client (lettuce -> lettuce 6.x compatibility shim) and Kafka consumer libs, with a smoke test suite exercising backpressure and rebalancing scenarios.

Scope & Non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on architecture + implementation for core runtime-topology changes. It does NOT change customer-facing Snake API or billing model.
- We will not change per-tenant quota enforcement in this ticket; quotas are handled upstream by the rate-limiter service.

Design decisions: 
- The new InflightManager interface exposes: allocate(tenant, units) -> boolean, release(tenant, units), snapshot(tenant) -> {outstanding, lastUpdate}. Implementation is credit-based so callers request credits and the manager returns an allowed amount. This prevents single large requests from blocking smaller ones.
- Circuit breaker triggers: rolling 30s window error-rate > 10% OR p95 processing latency > 500ms OR outstanding tasks > tenant-configured soft-limit. When tripped, the circuit marks tenant as degraded and reduces its default credit allotment by a factor. Admins can override via Console.
- Retry handling: retries are scheduled into an in-memory timer wheel per-node (coordinated via a lightweight Redis sorted-set fallback for cross-node handover). Retries carry idempotency keys; if a work item has a confirmed dedupe token, the retry is skipped. This reduces duplicate downstream work and simplifies failure semantics.
- Redis Streams: use group-level ack semantics and prefetch only when credits are available. For Kafka, maintain the same credit handshake but reuse the InflightManager and retry wheel.

Compatibility & migration:
- We will run both old and new worker loops in parallel behind a feature flag. Traffic for a small set of tenants will be routed to the new loop for verification. A migration plan and rollback steps are documented in the RFC.

Observability:
- New metrics: inflight.per_tenant.outstanding, inflight.per_tenant.credits_issued, circuitbreaker.per_tenant.state, retry.queue.length, retry.dropped_due_to_dedupe, head_of_line.latency_p95.
- Dashboards: add an "Ingress Fairness" dashboard in Console with per-tenant histograms and alerts on circuit trips.

Dependencies:
- A short RFC has been posted: https://go.redwood/rfcs/async-ingress-control (internal).
- Implementation PR will be: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/12459 (WIP).

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for InflightManager and circuit breaker covering allocation contention and trip/recover paths.
- Integration test showing no more than 10% tail latency regression under a mixed workload and that noisy-tenant credit throttling reduces impact on others.
- Smoke matrix validating Redis client upgrade under failover and rebalancing scenarios.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag + e2e tests.
2) Canary on 3 low-traffic tenants for 48 hours. Watch for increased retries or duplicate work.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% tenants, then full rollout if stable.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Using an in-memory timer wheel reduces cross-node Redis pressure but requires careful handover on agent restarts; we accept the complexity to get lower latency for retries.
- Per-tenant circuit breakers introduce potential fairness tuning complexity (too aggressive = customer impact), but we prefer conservative defaults and tooling for quick override.
comments: 2026-02-28 Aisha Patel: Triage - found elevated p95 for multi-tenant Redis stream ingestion after last client bump. Created ticket to decouple concerns and harden fairness.

2026-03-02 Marco Liu: Initial design proposal posted in RFC (linked in description). Chose credit-based model after benchmarking token-bucket vs credits; credits give smoother issuing for bursty small requests.

2026-03-04 Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed design. Asked for explicit plan for cross-node retry handover and durable visibility of pending retries in case of node crash. Suggested using Redis sorted-set only as fallback.
2026-03-06 Marco Liu: Implemented InflightManager prototype and benchmark harness. Local tests show 18% reduction in head-of-line p95 under mixed-size payloads. PR skeleton opened: #12459.
2026-03-08 Sven Johansson (Security): Flagged that tenant circuit-breaker state must be auditable and put into audit logs for compliance. Added requirement to write state transitions to audit stream.

2026-03-10 Marco Liu: Added metrics and dashboard draft. Noted that lettuce client upgrade required a small compatibility shim. Smoke tests for failover are passing locally; failing intermittently on CI with a race - investigating.

2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Blocker - CI intermittent failure reproduces on staging during Kafka consumer rebalance. Hypothesis: credit accounting race when rebalancing partitions. Added next action to instrument rebalancing path and add a cooperative pause/resume handshake.
2026-03-12 Marco Liu: Working on fix for rebalance race. ETA 2 days. Will update PR and add integration test that simulates consumer group rebalance during heavy ingress.
2026-03-12 Carlos Mendes (PM): Prioritizing this work for the Tenant Fairness initiative; allows moving to P1 and allocating an additional engineer for rebalance work if needed.
